title: Staged throttling + tenant-scoped fallbacks for cross-region Dedicated clusters
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: During regional degradation or upstream control-plane pressure, a single noisy tenant can cause global capacity storms that lead to SLA violations for other Dedicated customers. Current control-plane failover triggers a coarse global fallback which increases blast radius and causes upgrade churn. Goal: Implement tenant-scoped circuit breakers and a staged throttling/fallback policy that preserves per-tenant SLOs where possible while enabling graceful multi-region failover and safe control-plane upgrades for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope:
- Per-tenant rate and concurrency circuit breakers in the control-plane routing layer.
- Staged load-shedding policies (soft -> hard) that operate by tenant priority, request type (inference vs management), and inferred tail-latency trends.
- Cross-region failover orchestration that coordinates per-tenant state (KV cache invalidation, active model variant mappings) with minimal global disruption.
- Observability: rollout dashboards, per-tenant SLO dashboards, and eviction/deny logs for audits.

Requirements and acceptance criteria:
1) Define tenant SLO profiles (default & custom) and a mapping that control-plane uses to make shedding decisions.
2) Circuit breakers should be configurable per-tenant and support automatic half-open probing.
3) Staged shedding must first apply adaptive request queuing and slowpath routing, then soft throttling (token bucket reduction), and finally hard rejection with clear 429+X-RW-REASON headers.
4) Multi-region failover should be able to fail over individual tenants to secondary regions with KV pre-warm heuristics for hot prefixes; default behavior is tenant-local prefer + region-fallback.
5) During control-plane upgrades, tenants marked as sensitive must be drained with an automated staging window and a rollback plan.
6) Ensure audit logs and metrics are surfaced in Console: per-tenant shed rate, breaker trips, probe success rate, and SLO burn rates.
7) End-to-end test harness that simulates noisy tenants, partial region outages, and upgrade windows; validate no more than 1% increase in P99 latency for non-impacted tenants in typical degraded scenarios.

Non-goals: automatic model migration, changes to Dedicated GPU scheduling, customer billing changes.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Trade-off: aggressive per-tenant shedding reduces blast radius but increases churn for the noisy tenant; we prefer tenant-specific control over global kill-switches.
- Trade-off: cross-region per-tenant failover introduces complex state sync; we will use eventual consistency with pre-warm hints to limit cold-start latency.
- Safety: default breaker thresholds and shedding policies must be conservative; expose tuning knobs in Dedicated admin API for enterprise customers.

Deliverables:
- Control-plane changes for per-tenant circuit-breakers and staged throttles (runtime + admin API).
- Orchestration changes for region-fallback with per-tenant migration hooks.
- Console dashboards and auditing views.
- Test harness and chaos scenarios.
- Runbook for ops: detection, manual override, and post-incident analysis.
comments: 2026-02-17: Kickoff with Reliability/Platform. Agreed to implement three-stage shedding (queue -> soft throttle -> hard reject). Action: draft breaker API spec (owner: Luca).

2026-02-22: Spike results: per-tenant breaker adds ~2% control-plane CPU under load (bench on dev cluster). Decided to keep lightweight in-memory counters with sampled telemetry to reduce disk IO. Link to spike notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/TENANT-BREAKER-SPIKE

2026-02-26: Design review with PM and Security. Need explicit audit headers for GDPR and audit logs retention policy. Added security_review_required flag. Attaching PRD: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/dedicated-fallback-prd

2026-03-01: Implemented breaker + probe prototype in control-plane branch 'feat/tenant-breaker'. Created integration test for half-open behavior. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/2487

2026-03-03: Load test with synthetic noisy tenant (700% baseline) — observed successful isolation; some hard rejects occurred earlier than expected due to conservative probe window. Follow-up: tune probe backoff and expose probe window via admin API.
2026-03-05: Added Console mockups for per-tenant shed rate and breaker events. UX feedback: add timeline view and quick mute for on-call (feature request).
